verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.0: Climbing above the clouds, you can catch sight of meteors soaring through $(2)Verdant Sky$(). $(p)There is nobody except yourself. There might be some pebbles or water, but what if there aren't? $(p)Fortunately, plants will always keep you company~
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.1: $(2)Verdant Sky$() is a harsher Botania skyblock than $(thing)Garden of Glass$(). It is only suitable for masochists familiar with vanilla mechanics and Botania. Of course, even if you know nothing about them, it won't stop you from experiencing it. $(p)It does not modify Botania (unless certain tweaks are enabled). It mainly builds upon the progression of $(thing)Garden of Glass$() by providing alternative methods to deal with the lack of water and stone.
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.2: After creating a Void world, you can use trees to craft a $(item)Composter$() and obtain $(item)Bone Meal$() and $(l:basics/flowers)$(item)Floral Fertilizer$(0)$(/l). There is no water source here, so your $(item)Petal Apothecary$() can only wait for rain to get water. If it doesn't rain, you might have to travel to a place where it does, or find other methods, such as using the $(l:basics/corrupt_belladonna)$(item)Corrupt Belladonna$(0)$(/l).
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.3: Perhaps the environment does not allow you to obtain $(item)Cobblestone$() (or you find it unreasonable to sift infinite $(item)Pebbles$() from soil). In that case, you can use $(item)Wooden Planks$() to craft Wooden Petal Apothecaries and Wooden Cauldrons, and use $(item)Livingwood$() to craft a $(item)Livingwood Mana Pool$(). Use them as temporary substitutes for now, and consider obtaining stone later.
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.4: Crafting an $(item)Oak Petal Apothecary$(). Other wood types have their corresponding Apothecaries.
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.5: Crafting an $(item)Oak Cauldron$(). Other wood types have their corresponding Cauldrons.
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.6: Crafting a $(item)Livingwood Mana Pool$(). Its capacity is equivalent to a $(l:mana/pool)$(item)Diluted Mana Pool$(0)$(/l).
verdant_sky.page.verdant_sky.7: In addition, $(2)Verdant Sky$() provides new Miscellaneous Flowers, Generating Flowers, and Functional Flowers. For example, the $(l:basics/corrupt_belladonna)$(item)Corrupt Belladonna$(0)$(/l) and $(l:functional_flowers/decay_agapanthus)$(item)Decay Agapanthus$(0)$(/l) can turn Leaves into Dirt, and the $(l:generating_flowers/drinking_snow_lotus)$(item)Drinking Snow Lotus$(0)$(/l) can consume snow to produce Mana, etc. However, it is clear that you will have to explore and think for yourself to figure out the proper uses for most of these new plants.
verdant_sky.tagline.corrupt_belladonna: Reverse version of the Pure Daisy
verdant_sky.page.corrupt_belladonna.0: The $(item)Corrupt Belladonna$() is an important flower. $(p)Give this flower a minute, and it will decay any nearby $(item)Leaves$() and other blocks into their decayed counterparts, $(item)Dirt$() and more. It provides ways to obtain and regenerate some materials in special environments.
verdant_sky.page.corrupt_belladonna.1: A few other blocks can also be decayed by this flower, some of which require specific environments. These recipes aren't as important as Dirt, but they can still be useful in certain situations. For example, if you are short on water but have some snow, you can decay $(item)Snow Blocks$() into $(item)Water$().
verdant_sky.page.corrupt_belladonna.2: Here is a list of all possible conversions:$(li)$(item)Leaves$() decays into $(item)Dirt$() $(li)$(item)Snow Blocks$() decays into $(item)Water$() $(li)$(item)Livingwood Logs$() decays into $(item)Oak Logs$() $(li)$(item)Livingrock$() decays into $(item)Stone$() $(li)$(item)Blue Ice$() decays into $(item)Packed Ice$() $(li)$(item)Packed Ice$() decays into $(item)Ice$() $(li)$(item)Obsidian$() decays into $(item)Crying Obsidian$() $(p)In the Nether:$(li)$(item)Cobblestone$() decays into $(item)Netherrack$() $(li)$(item)Sand$() decays into $(item)Soul Sand$() $(p)In the End:$(li)$(item)Cobbled Deepslate$() decays into $(item)End Stone$()
verdant_sky.page.corrupt_belladonna.3: You must corrupt the world of this purity.
verdant_sky.tagline.decay_agapanthus: Enhanced version of the Corrupt Belladonna
verdant_sky.page.decay_agapanthus.0: $(item)Decay Agapanthus$() is a $(thing)Functional Flower$(0) that serves as the enhanced version to the Corrupt Belladonna. It consumes $(thing)Mana$(0) to operate, but it works faster and covers a larger radius. $(p)It can be toggled on and off using a $(thing)Redstone signal$(0). $(p)Beware of its side effects: when it successfully decays a block, it applies the $(thing)Wither effect$(0) to nearby mobs.
verdant_sky.page.decay_agapanthus.3: $(o)...Though turned to mud, they'd nurture flowers' growth next spring.$()
verdant_sky.page.drinking_snow_lotus.0: $(item)Drinking Snow Lotus$() is a $(thing)Generating Flower$() that loves ice and snow. It devours Snowballs, Snow, and Snow Blocks on the ground to continuously produce $(thing)Mana$(). The more it drinks, the longer it works.$(p)If placed in a $(thing)Cold Biome$(), its efficiency increases several times. This is a privilege of flowers blessed by ice and snow.
verdant_sky.page.drinking_snow_lotus.1: When the Drinking Snow Lotus devours different snow resources, its fullness and the provided work time vary:$(li)$(item)Snow Block$(): most filling, provides 8s each$(li)$(item)Snow$(): comes next, provides 4s each$(li)$(item)Snowball$(): least filling, provides 2s each.$(p)Note that once fully fed, the lotus will no longer want to drink. If it is $(thing)snowing$(), it will also drink the snowflakes falling from the sky.
verdant_sky.page.drinking_snow_lotus.2: The Drinking Snow Lotus devours dropped items very frequently, making it hard to control the timing of feeding. Therefore, manual management is not recommended.$(p)A Comparator can output a Redstone signal based on its remaining working time, outputting 1 signal strength for every 120 Snowballs. Using a timer to drop snowballs near it at regular intervals is also one of the ideal ways to automate it.
